turns.content: Treat the incoming object as a photon moving at 12 km/s and retain the asteroid-impact calculation.
Using the physical model and approximation established above, write the corresponding conserved-quantity equation for the approach, neglecting atmospheric drag and Earth recoil.
Rearrange the energy equation to isolate the final refractive index squared.
Substitute the radii established at the outset into the equation just obtained and simplify the dimensionless coefficient multiplying its physical interaction scale.
Use the simplified energy result to calculate an orbital period in km/s and m/s.
Report the result, state the approximation used, and identify any Earth-recoil uncertainty that cannot be quantified from the given parameters.
Check the sign of the gravitational interaction-energy change and whether the numerical result has the expected scale under the fixed-Earth model.
Give the final speed together with the approximation used to obtain it.
